messages:
Priya: FYI wegot a partner onboarding request that involves them uploading encrypted config blobs to our S3 bucket. They used sops with a GCP KMS key under their project and asked us to rewrap to our CMEK and store in Vault. Need advice on RBAC + audit and a safe rotation plan.
Daniel: quick clarification: are these partner-managed keys or do they want us to grant our KMS key to their SA?
Priya: They generated ciphertexts using their projects/partner-proj KMS key and want us to decrypt+rewrap. They can provide the ciphertext and we will store rewrapped blobs in Vault at secret/partners/<org>/config.
Ivy: ok, so we only need decrypt access to their key version. That requires cross-project IAM @ key version level. Preferably they create a short-lived service account we can impersonate. Never grant broad project roles.
Alex: Also confirm the legal/contract side: do we have consent to hold their plaintext? If yes, treat them as customer data and apply tighter retention.
Priya: legal signoff is in the ticket. They explicitly allowed rewrap for migration.
Daniel: proposed flow: 1) partner gives us ciphertext package + KMS resource name + key version id; 2) we create a temporary import transient SA in our infra project that is granted roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the partner SA (impersonation) OR partner grants our collector-service@ourproj a single keyDecrypt binding on that cryptoKeyVersion; 3) run rewrap job in staging; 4) store output in Vault transit/ or kv depending on use-case; 5) destroy temp keys and record audit.
Ivy: I'm nervous about impersonation across tenants. Simpler: partner grants our dedicated `importer-sa@ourproj` keyDecrypt on the specific cryptoKeyVersion only. We restrict via IAM Condition to the exact cryptoKey resource name.
Priya: Good. We'll ask for that. Also we need to capture audit logs for every decrypt operation and ship them to security SIEM. Can we enforce CMEK audit logs retention 90d for this project?
Alex: We can include the partner project in our centralized logging sink, but partners often don't allow that. Alternative: ask partner to grant us view access to their logging bucket or set up a push sink to our BQ dataset. Need to confirm.
Daniel: regardless, our side should log a rewrap event with metadata: partner org, source key, source key version, operator SA, job id, and pre/post checksum. That's the minimum for forensics.
Ivy: runbook snippets: to decrypt from KMS and re-encrypt with our key via gcloud:
```bash
# decrypt with partner key (assuming importer-sa has decrypt permission)
gcloud kms decrypt \
  --location=global \
  --keyring=partner-ring \
  --key=partner-key \
  --ciphertext-file=blob.ctxt \
  --plaintext-file=blob.plain \

# re-encrypt with our CMEK
gcloud kms encrypt \
  --location=us \ 
  --keyring=redwood-keys \
  --key=redwood-cmek \
  --plaintext-file=blob.plain \
  --ciphertext-file=blob.rewrapped
```
Priya: For Vault storage we will use transit wrap to add an extra envelope:
```bash
vault write transit/encrypt/partners-<org> plaintext=$(base64 < blob.rewrapped)
```
Alex: Important: do not keep plaintext on disk longer than necessary. Use in-memory pipelines in the rewrap job, and delete blobs after verifying checksum. Add a shred step in the job.
Daniel: Rotation/retention policy: since these are imported artifacts, mark them with metadata `rotated_from=partner-key:v123` and create a scheduled job to rotate to our active key within 7 days. After rotation and verification destroy the imported ciphertexts versioned backup after 30d.
Ivy: Add: if partner later revokes decrypt permission, we must have re-encrypted everything prior to revocation. Request a revocation notice window in the contract (48-72h).
Priya: Security asks that we run an initial canary on a non-production org first. Plan to run rewrap job in staging for one partner org tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Need approvals from Ops and SRE.
ops-bot: Request created: infra/rewrap-job-78, assigned to Daniel. CI pipeline scheduled. ETA 3h.
Alex: Also check sops metadata: some sops files contain KMS key ARNs in comments and backups elsewhere. We need to find any leaked copies in repo history. @Priya grep for `sops` and `partner-key` across our monorepos and backup buckets.
Priya: Will run grep and open GH issue with matches. Also will ask partner to sign a short-lived KMS grant YAML like:
```yaml
bindings:
  - role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
    members:
      - serviceAccount:importer-sa@ourproj.iam.gserviceaccount.com
    condition:
      title: "importer-only"
      expression: "resource.name == 'projects/partner-proj/locations/global/keyRings/partner-ring/cryptoKeys/partner-key/cryptoKeyVersions/1'"
```
Daniel: Terraform snippet for our side (key in our project):
```hcl
resource "google_kms_crypto_key" "redwood_import_alias" {
  name = "imported-partner-<org>"
  key_ring = "projects/ourproj/locations/us/keyRings/redwood"
  rotation_period = "7776000s" # 90d
}
```
Ivy: Add SIEM events mapping: CryptoKeyDecrypt -> event.type = "rewrap.decrypt" with labels partner_org, source_key, job_id. Ensure logs forwarded to BQ dataset `security_audit.crypto` and alert if decrypt count > 100 within 1h.
Priya: I'll draft the PR with infra job, logging hooks, and the canary plan. Tag reviewers: @Ivy @Daniel @Alex.
ops-bot: PR opened: infra/PR-7890 by Priya. Pipeline: tests running.
Daniel: For rollback include commands to revoke importer-sa binding and to rewrap back to partner key if needed. Example revoke:
```bash
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/partner-proj/locations/global/keyRings/partner-ring/cryptoKeys/partner-key \
  --member=\"serviceAccount:importer-sa@ourproj.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" \
  --role=\"roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter\"
```
Ivy: Post-deploy checks: - confirm no broad roles granted in partner project - verify audit log entries for every decrypt - verify Vault stored blob has metadata and checksum - schedule rotation ticket.
Priya: thanks. Will post canary results in this thread tomorrow.
ops-bot: Pipeline passed. Canary started. Test decrypt count: 3, errors: 0. ETA: monitor 24h.
